templates.name: Addition/similarity: a further item of the same kind
Contrast: established view or appearance, then a finding that breaks it
Contrast: positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence
Cause/effect: need or judgment, then the action it motivates
Concession: grant, then the main claim resumes (but / Still)
Concession: supported claim, then a fact that qualifies it
Purpose and aptness: goal then deliberate act, or a fitting echo
Specification/restatement: exact content or plain rewording
Sequence/time: next step, earlier or later event, end of a long effort
Culmination, alternative and place (ultimately, alternatively, there)
Example: general claim, then one named instance

items.passage: Boro, the cotton garments and bedcovers that poor families in northern Japan patched and repatched over generations, now hang in art museums. ______ the farmers who stitched them were mending, not composing, since new fabric was too expensive to waste. Yet the overlapping patches, faded to uneven shades of indigo, form abstract compositions that critics have compared to modernist painting.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says boro are now displayed as art. The blank sentence concedes a point that seems to work against that status: the people who made boro were only mending cloth, not trying to make art. The next sentence, beginning with “Yet,” returns to the main claim by describing the patches’ artistic effect. “Granted” signals this kind of concession before a turn.

A.why_wrong: Boro hanging in museums did not cause the farmers to mend rather than compose; the mending came first, and it is a point that cuts against the textiles’ status as art.

C.why_wrong: The farmers’ mending is not an instance of boro being shown in museums; it is a fact that seems to count against treating boro as art.

D.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add a point in favor of boro as art, but the farmers’ lack of artistic aims is a concession, which the sentence beginning with “Yet” then answers.

items.notes: Plan band_target 6. Grant-then-turn frame with the turn carried by a following “Yet” (3.19 uses “Still”, b1 used “Still”, 3.17 uses “but”). No contrast decoy (contrast next to a concession key reads as acceptable). Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (brief of 2026-10-16).

review.notes: No fact check (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation. Second-sense check: no emphasis or corrective decoy (no In fact, Indeed, Actually); Consequently, For instance and Moreover each make a false claim about the grant.

band7.why: K1_grant_turn has no band-7 official items (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md); grant then Yet is the band-6 K1 pattern (3.17, 3.19). Strong band 6: rare key, no contrast decoy, the turn sits a sentence after the blank.

items.passage: Economists examined the records of a large US company that had begun enrolling new employees in its retirement savings plan automatically. Among new hires, participation rose from 37 percent to 86 percent. ______ most automatically enrolled employees contributed just 3 percent of their salaries, the plan’s default, far less than many earlier hires had chosen voluntarily.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first two sentences report a clear success: automatic enrollment raised participation among new hires from 37 percent to 86 percent. The blank sentence adds a fact that limits that success without denying it: most of the new participants saved just 3 percent of their salaries, far less than many earlier employees had chosen. “That said” introduces a qualification of this kind.

A.why_wrong: The sentence does not give the precise details of the rise in participation; it turns to how much the new participants saved, a fact that limits the success.

B.why_wrong: “Indeed” would introduce a fact that confirms or strengthens the previous point, but low contributions do not strengthen the finding that participation rose; they qualify it.

C.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add another point in the policy’s favor, but contributions “far less” than earlier hires chose count against its success.

items.notes: Real study (Madrian and Shea 2001, The Power of Suggestion): new-hire participation 37% to 86% under automatic enrollment; most kept the 3% default although earlier participants commonly chose higher rates. Names left out (a famous field study retold with named authors is a judge tell). Band-7 checks (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md section 6): key not in the core 13, pass; no sequence or summary decoy, pass; surface-contrast proxy not applicable (adversative key, as in the band-7 K2 model 3.12); register about 5.8 chars/word, pass; trap annotation: B, read alone, looks like an elaboration of A (same people, another percentage), not a limit. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (brief of 2026-10-16).
band7_moves: same referent: B is about the same automatically enrolled new hires and gives a figure, so Specifically reads on a first pass as a detail of A
the limit is carried by stance words (just, far less) rather than an explicit contrast marker
A stays true (participation did rise), so B qualifies rather than corrects; the emphasis decoy is Indeed rather than In fact, which has a corrective sense
no phantom-sequence or summary decoy; no cause decoy, since default inertia would make a causal link arguable

review.notes: No fact check (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation. Second-sense check: Indeed beside That said kept; unlike In fact it has no corrective (actually, contrary to that) sense, and CB offers Indeed beside a concession key (fb56b593, Granted). Cause decoy correctly avoided (the 3 percent default does cause the low rates).

band7.why: Mirrors the band-7 K2 item ecb31049 (positive record, then a limiting fact, key That said, Moreover and Specifically decoys) with the arguable cause decoy dropped; register about 5.8 chars/word; B names the same new hires and gives another figure, so Specifically pulls on a first read, and the limit is carried only by stance words (just, far less).

items.passage: Argentine writer Victoria Ocampo was convinced that Latin American literature would be enriched by sustained contact with writing from other parts of the world. ______ in 1931 she founded Sur, a magazine that for four decades published new work by Latin American authors alongside Spanish translations of European and North American writers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence states Ocampo’s conviction that Latin American literature would benefit from contact with writing from elsewhere. The blank sentence describes an action she took to bring about that contact: founding a magazine that printed Latin American work next to translations of foreign writers. “To that end” signals that an action serves a goal just described.

B.why_wrong: Founding Sur was not an alternative to, or a departure from, Ocampo’s conviction; it put that conviction into practice.

C.why_wrong: The sentence does not reword Ocampo’s belief; it reports an action she took to act on it.

D.why_wrong: “Furthermore” would present the magazine as a separate, additional point, but founding Sur was the means by which Ocampo pursued the goal in the first sentence.

items.passage: Nearly all birds incubate their eggs with their own body heat. During the breeding season, many develop a brood patch, a featherless, blood-vessel-rich area of skin that warms the clutch. ______ megapodes, ground-dwelling birds of Australasia, bury their eggs in mounds of rotting vegetation or volcanically heated soil, relying entirely on the heat of decomposition or geothermal activity.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first two sentences say that nearly all birds warm their eggs with their own bodies, often through a brood patch. The blank sentence says megapodes do the opposite: they bury their eggs and let heat from rotting plants or the ground warm them. “In contrast” signals this difference between most birds and megapodes.

A.why_wrong: Megapodes are birds, but they are an exception to the pattern in the first two sentences, not an instance of it.

B.why_wrong: Megapodes do not warm their eggs the way other birds do; their method is the opposite one.

D.why_wrong: Other birds’ use of body heat does not cause megapodes to bury their eggs.

items.passage: Woodcut is a relief printing technique: the printmaker carves away the portions of a wooden block intended to remain blank, and ink is applied to the protruding surfaces that remain. items.explanation: The first sentence explains that in a woodcut the ink sits on the raised parts of the block. The second explains that in an engraving the ink sits in lines cut into the plate. Because the two printing methods work in opposite ways, “by contrast” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The sentence about engraving does not restate how woodcuts work; it describes a different method that works the opposite way.

B.why_wrong: Engraving is not an instance of woodcut; it is a different kind of printmaking.

B.why_wrong: The visitors’ claim did not cause the excavations’ finding; the finding goes against the claim.

C.why_wrong: The excavations’ finding is not like the visitors’ claim; it shows that the claim was wrong.

D.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not reword the visitors’ claim; it contradicts it.
